source_excerpt: Plus: $10/user/mo ($8 billed annually). Pro: $20/user/mo ($15 billed annually). Business: $40/seat/mo ($480 billed annually).
observation: Gamma publishes self-serve tiers: Free ($0, 400 credits), Plus ($10/user/month or $8 annual), Pro ($20/user/month or $15 annual), and Business ($40/seat/month billed annually at $480/seat/year).
interpretation: Mainstream AI presentation tools anchor individual/team pricing between $10 and $20 per user per month, with business-tier governance reaching $40 per user per month.

source_excerpt: When exporting to PowerPoint, tables are exported as editable objects by default... Gamma uses flexible cards rather than fixed slides.
observation: Gamma documents that it exports documents to PPTX format with editable tables, but notes that Gamma uses a responsive card layout rather than fixed slide dimensions, meaning elements and complex layouts do not map 1:1 to standard PowerPoint slide templates.
interpretation: Gamma produces slide-like cards rather than native PowerPoint decks, requiring users to manually reformat and re-align content when exported to PPTX.

source_excerpt: Pro: $12/mo billed annually ($144/yr), or $45/mo billed monthly. Team: $40/user/mo billed annually. Enterprise: Custom quote.
observation: Beautiful.ai charges $12 per month billed annually ($144/year) or $45 billed monthly for its Pro plan, and $40 per user per month billed annually for its Team plan with shared brand controls.
interpretation: Team collaboration with brand controls commands $40 per user per month, whereas individual subscriptions sit around $12 to $15 per month annually.

source_excerpt: Export to editable PowerPoint is available on Pro, Team, and Enterprise... animations and dynamic layout rules do not carry over.
observation: Beautiful.ai allows exporting presentations as editable PPTX files on Pro and Team plans, but notes that its proprietary smart-slide layout engine rules, transitions, and animations do not carry over into PowerPoint.
interpretation: Once exported to PowerPoint, the smart dynamic layout constraints are lost, converting the deck into static PowerPoint shapes and text boxes that can break during subsequent client edits.

source_excerpt: Basic: $15/user/mo. Pro: $25/user/mo ($20 billed annually). Enterprise: Custom quote with custom template integration.
observation: Plus AI operates as an add-in inside PowerPoint and Google Slides, with pricing at $15/user/month (Basic), $25/user/month or $20 annual (Pro), and custom pricing for Enterprise.
interpretation: Plus AI demonstrates that an in-tool PowerPoint add-in can charge $20 to $25 per user per month for individual/team AI generation.

source_excerpt: Custom template uploads are in beta for simple layouts. Complex enterprise templates with charts and custom master layouts require white-glove setup.
observation: Plus AI documentation states that custom template upload is in beta (primarily for Google Slides) and optimized for basic text/image layouts; complex branded templates with custom charts and master layouts require white-glove onboarding on Enterprise plans.
interpretation: Self-serve AI presentation add-ins struggle to automatically map generated content to complex corporate PowerPoint master layouts without human professional services.

source_excerpt: Microsoft 365 Copilot is available as an add-on for $30 per user per month with an annual commitment.
observation: Microsoft charges $30 per user per month with an annual commitment for Microsoft 365 Copilot, which operates across PowerPoint, Word, Excel, and Teams, requiring a qualifying base Microsoft 365 license.
interpretation: Microsoft has anchored official enterprise AI suite pricing at $30 per user per month, creating a ceiling for generic AI features bundled into Office.

source_excerpt: When creating a presentation from a file, Copilot supports referencing only a single file at a time, and additional prompt context cannot be added within the same prompt.
observation: Microsoft's official documentation for Copilot in PowerPoint states that creating a presentation from a file is limited to referencing a single file at a time (e.g. one Word document under 24MB), and users cannot append additional prompt instructions in the same command.
interpretation: Copilot cannot execute a multi-input sales deck workflow (e.g., combining CRM opportunity notes + customer case studies + master deck template) in a single automated step.

source_excerpt: Free: $0. Plus: $17/seat/mo ($14 billed annually). Pro: $28/seat/mo ($22 billed annually).
observation: Pitch prices its presentation platform at Free ($0 for 2 editors), Plus ($17/seat/month or $14 annual), and Pro ($28/seat/month or $22 annual) with shared team workspace and analytics.
interpretation: Pitch provides collaborative presentation authoring at $17 to $28 per seat per month, positioning itself as a modern browser alternative to Google Slides.

source_excerpt: Export presentations to .pptx files on paid plans. Note that video embeds, dynamic interactions, and proprietary fonts may not transfer identically.
observation: Pitch allows exporting presentations to .pptx on paid plans, but documents that interactive web widgets, embedded videos, and web fonts do not transfer into PowerPoint without loss of fidelity.
interpretation: Pitch prioritizes online sharing via web links; PPTX export is a secondary fallback with fidelity degradation.

source_excerpt: Automatically pull CRM data into presentations and business-review decks from Salesforce and HubSpot. Generate and send personalized Storydocs without manual copy-pasting.
icp: B2B Sales Teams, Account Executives, RevOps
observation: Storydoc integrates natively with Salesforce and HubSpot to dynamically populate customer-specific presentations from CRM fields without manual copy-paste, tracking viewer engagement in real time.
interpretation: Storydoc represents an existing complete workflow substitute for automated customer-specific sales collateral using CRM data, but in an interactive web format rather than PowerPoint.

source_excerpt: Storydoc does not support direct export to PowerPoint (.pptx). Exports are available as static PDF documents only.
observation: Storydoc documentation explicitly states that it does not support exporting presentations to native editable PowerPoint (.pptx) format, offering only static PDF downloads or hosted interactive links.
interpretation: Storydoc cannot serve B2B buyers whose corporate procurement, security, or enterprise clients strictly require native editable .pptx files.

source_excerpt: Teams plan priced at $40 per user/month for up to 25 seats. Enterprise plan custom priced. Integrates inside PowerPoint and Salesforce.
observation: Templafy offers a PowerPoint add-in that automates template governance, brand compliance, and dynamic slide generation pulling from Salesforce, with a entry Teams plan at $40 per user per month.
interpretation: Templafy proves willingness to pay $40/user/mo for template-compliant PowerPoint generation, but is tailored toward corporate IT governance rather than solo-founder SMB adoption.

source_excerpt: UpSlide helps finance and consulting teams automate PowerPoint formatting, manage approved slide libraries, and dynamically link Excel data to PowerPoint presentations.
observation: UpSlide provides a dedicated Microsoft Office add-in for consulting and financial firms that manages pre-approved slide libraries, enforces corporate brand formatting, and automates Excel-to-PPT linking.
interpretation: High-value professional services already rely on PowerPoint add-ins for brand consistency and deck assembly, validating that template compliance inside PowerPoint is commercially viable.

source_excerpt: AutoDocs allows revenue teams to generate personalized presentations automatically using marketing-approved templates and data from Salesforce or Dynamics.
observation: Highspot's AutoDocs module automates the generation of customized presentation decks from marketing-approved PowerPoint templates populated with dynamic customer CRM data from Salesforce or Microsoft Dynamics.
interpretation: The exact workflow of generating personalized presentations from approved templates using CRM inputs is already solved natively by enterprise sales enablement platforms.

source_excerpt: Highspot contracts typically range from $70,000 to $180,000+ per year, with per-user costs between $45 and $65/user/month and minimum seat thresholds of 50+ users.
observation: Procurement benchmarks report that Highspot requires annual contracts typically ranging from $70,000 to $180,000+ ($45-$65/user/month), with implementation services costing $5,000 to $50,000 and minimum 50+ seat commitments.
interpretation: While enterprise platforms solve deck automation, their high annual contract floor ($70k+) creates an unserved SMB/mid-market gap for smaller teams unable to procure Highspot.

source_excerpt: LiveDocs for PowerPoint enables teams to build dynamic templates with placeholders that automatically assemble prospect-specific pitch decks from Salesforce data.
observation: Seismic LiveDocs provides a PowerPoint plugin that allows marketing to configure dynamic templates with rules and placeholders, automatically generating personalized pitch decks using live Salesforce CRM data.
interpretation: Seismic offers an end-to-end dynamic PowerPoint deck automation engine connected to CRM, functioning as an established direct substitute for large enterprise revenue teams.

source_excerpt: When downloading presentations as PPTX, formatting, fonts, and text box spacing can change due to rendering differences between Canva and PowerPoint.
observation: Canva's official help guides document that downloading presentations as PPTX format commonly causes font substitutions, text reflow, and element misalignment due to discrepancies between browser rendering and PowerPoint engines.
interpretation: Horizontal design tools cannot reliably replace native PowerPoint authoring because cross-platform conversion frequently introduces visual bugs that require manual repolishing.

source_excerpt: Think-cell annual subscriptions cost approximately $260 to $325 per user per year for consulting and corporate teams automating PowerPoint charts and layouts.
observation: Procurement data shows think-cell licenses cost $260 to $325 per user per year (approx $22-$27/month equivalent) for PowerPoint add-in software that automates chart building and slide layout from Excel/JSON.
interpretation: Demonstrates consistent willingness to pay $20+ per user per month for specialized software that lives directly inside PowerPoint to automate slide production.

source_excerpt: Tome discontinued its viral AI presentation generator on April 30, 2025, deleting user decks and pivoting to enterprise CRM under the name Lightfield.
observation: VentureBeat reported that Tome officially shut down its generative AI presentation product on April 30, 2025 and pivoted to Lightfield (an AI CRM) after failing to achieve sustainable enterprise monetization despite 20M users.
interpretation: Highlights structural risk that broad, horizontal AI presentation generators face commoditization and low retention if they cannot embed deeply into enterprise workflows or deliver corporate-grade output.

source_excerpt: Starter: $35/user/month. Growth: $275/month. Scale: $750/month. Create interactive web sales documents and proposals.
observation: Qwilr prices its interactive sales proposal software at $35 per user per month (Starter) and $275/month (Growth), explicitly marketing itself as a replacement for PowerPoint presentations and static PDFs.
interpretation: Reveals existing SMB willingness to pay $35/user/month for sales collateral automation, while attempting to displace PowerPoint with interactive web links.
